info.title: SoroTrail API
info.description:
A contract event indexer for the Stellar/Soroban network. SoroTrail polls
a Stellar RPC endpoint, stores contract events durably in Postgres, and
serves them back through a queryable HTTP API long after the RPC has
forgotten them.

JSON-producing operations accept the shared `pretty=true` query
parameter to indent responses for human inspection; it does not change
the response data.

get.description: Report whether the API process can reach its database and RPC dependencies. This probe is public and does not expose tenant data.

Paginated list of stored events, filterable by contract, type, topic,
ledger range, time range, and sort order. Supports cursor-based
pagination, field/XDR projections, and optional spec-driven enrichment.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of events matching the request's filters, ignoring pagination. Omitted when the count could not be computed; the page itself is still returned.

schema.description: One JSON event per line when stream=true.

delete.description: Deletes stored events matching the given bounds. Intended for retention maintenance; gated behind the management credential.

parameters.name: before_ledger
parameters.description: Delete every stored event in a ledger strictly below this one. Required: without it the request is refused rather than defaulting to a bound that would delete everything.

get.summary: Get a single event by ID
get.description: Return one stored event. The decoded parameter controls optional spec-driven enrichment, while include_xdr returns the stored XDR projection instead of decoded columns.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: TOID-based event identifier: the 16-digit ledger/transaction/ operation offset, a hyphen, and a 10-digit index within the operation. Take it from an event in a listing rather than composing it.

get.description: Convenience wrapper around GET /events with contract_id={id}. It accepts the same filters, pagination controls and response projections as the general event listing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract whose events to return.

200.description: A page of events for the contract

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of events matching the request's filters, ignoring pagination. Omitted when the count could not be computed; the page itself is still returned.

get.description: Events where the given Stellar address appears in the event topics, as either sender or recipient. Backed by the address activity index.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Stellar account (G-prefixed) or contract (C-prefixed) address to look for in the event topics.

parameters.name: order_by
parameters.description: Address activity is always ordered by event ID; this is the only accepted value.

200.description: A page of events involving the address

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of address events. The count endpoint used by the handler does not apply optional filters, so use the page's cursor for reliable filtered traversal.

get.description: Aggregate view of an address's activity: first and last ledger it was seen in, total event count, and the distinct contracts it interacted with.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Stellar account (G-prefixed) or contract (C-prefixed) address to summarise.

post.summary: Issue an API key for a tenant
post.description: Administrative endpoint, available only when MULTI_TENANT is enabled and gated behind the admin credential. The plaintext tenant key is returned only in this response.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Tenant ID, as returned by POST /admin/tenants. Must be a positive integer.

delete.description: Administrative endpoint, available only when MULTI_TENANT is enabled and gated behind the admin credential.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: API key ID, as returned by POST /admin/tenants/{id}/keys. This is the key's database ID, not its public prefix and not the plaintext key.

get.description:
Returns the metadata for every global API key on this instance. The plaintext key is never returned — it is visible only in the response to POST /apikeys, at creation time.
This endpoint is authenticated regardless of API_KEY_AUTH_ENABLED: an unauthenticated key-management surface would let any caller mint a key and bypass authentication entirely. The first key is issued out of band with `sorotrail apikey`.

post.description:
Mints a new global API key and returns it. The `key` field in the response is the only time the plaintext key is ever available — only a bcrypt hash of its secret half is persisted, so a lost key cannot be recovered and must be revoked and reissued.
The request body is optional; omitting it creates an unnamed key.

key.description: The plaintext key, in the form `sorotrail_<16-hex-prefix>_<64-hex-secret>`. Returned once and never again; store it before discarding the response.

delete.description: Marks the global key revoked. The row is kept so the key's history stays auditable, but the key stops authenticating immediately. Revoking an already-revoked key is not an error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The key's database ID, as returned by POST /apikeys — not its public prefix and not the plaintext key. Must be a positive integer.

get.description: Contracts that have at least one stored event, with per-contract event counts and ledger ranges. Ordered by contract_id ascending; pass sort=count to rank by activity instead. Paginated with an opaque cursor that is omitted on the last page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Ordering key for the listing. The default walks contract IDs alphabetically, which is stable as new contracts are indexed; count ranks by activity instead.

parameters.name: contract_id
parameters.description: Only list contracts whose ID starts with this prefix. A prefix, not a whole ID, so it is not validated as a strkey and a short string is a legitimate value.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of contracts matching the request's filters, ignoring pagination. Omitted when the count could not be computed; the page itself is still returned.

get.description: Reports only that the process is up. Never touches the database or RPC. It therefore has no failure response: a process that cannot answer 200 here cannot answer at all.
Reports whether the database, RPC and schema are usable, and whether ingestion has fallen more than 100 ledgers behind the chain head.

200.description: Every dependency is usable and ingestion is current

503.description: A dependency is unusable or ingestion is lagging. The body names the failing check so the instance can be pulled from the load balancer without reading the logs. This is a degraded-readiness report rather than the shared error envelope.

get.description: Version, commit and build date embedded at build time.
Prometheus text-format exposition of ingest, RPC and HTTP metrics. Exempt from rate limiting, so a scrape can never be throttled by the pressure it is there to measure.
Total number of events matching the filter, ignoring pagination.
Event counts bucketed by ledger or by a time interval.

parameters.name: bucket
parameters.description: Grouping interval. Either the literal "ledger", which counts events per ledger, or a Go duration string, which counts them per interval of wall-clock time. Required: there is no default grouping to fall back on.

get.description: Streaming CSV export of matching events. Pagination controls are intentionally ignored; the server walks the complete result set.

200.description: CSV rows streamed until the complete result set is written.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename for the generated CSV.

Cache-Control.description: Caching policy for the streamed export.

schema.description: CSV text with id, ledger, type, tx_hash, topics and value columns.

get.description: The base64 XDR the event was decoded from, for re-decoding.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: TOID-based event identifier: the 16-digit ledger/transaction/ operation offset, a hyphen, and a 10-digit index within the operation. Take it from an event in a listing rather than composing it.

get.description: Other events emitted by the same transaction.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: TOID-based event identifier: the 16-digit ledger/transaction/ operation offset, a hyphen, and a 10-digit index within the operation. Take it from an event in a listing rather than composing it.

get.description: Aggregate row for one indexed contract: how many events it has, the ledger range they span, and when it was last seen. Returns 404 for a contract with no indexed events.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract to describe.

event_count.description: Number of stored events for this contract

first_ledger.description: Earliest ledger holding an event for this contract

last_ledger.description: Most recent ledger holding an event for this contract

last_seen.description: Timestamp of the most recent event

get.description: Event count for one contract, plus cached token metadata (name, symbol, decimals) when the contract has been resolved as a token. The metadata fields are omitted for contracts with no cached metadata.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract to describe.

name.description: Token name, when cached metadata is available

symbol.description: Token symbol, when cached metadata is available

decimals.description: Token decimals, when cached metadata is available

event_count.description: Number of stored events for this contract

type_breakdown.description: Per-type event counts for this contract. Omitted when the breakdown is unavailable.

type.description: Event type, e.g. contract or diagnostic

count.description: Number of events of this type

get.description: Streaming export of every stored event for one contract.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract whose events to export.

parameters.name: from_ledger
parameters.description: Inclusive lower ledger bound. Required, and must not be greater than to_ledger. Unlike the list endpoints the export refuses an open-ended range outright, so a missing bound cannot drain the database one stream at a time.

parameters.name: to_ledger
parameters.description: Inclusive upper ledger bound. Required. The span it forms with from_ledger is capped by the EXPORT_MAX_RANGE environment variable, so a wide range may be refused by a deployment even though both bounds are individually valid.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Serialisation of the exported stream. The value is matched case-insensitively after surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment filename containing the contract and ledger range.

Cache-Control.description: Caching policy for the streamed export.

schema.description: One JSON event per line when format=ndjson.

put.description: Stores a user-supplied contract spec (SEP-0041 JSON) for a contract that exposes no fetchable spec. The enricher prefers the override over the RPC-fetched spec whenever one exists. Send the JSON body as {"spec": {...}}.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract whose spec is being overridden.

get.description: Returns the stored spec override for a contract, or 404 when none has been uploaded.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract whose spec override is being read.

delete.description: Removes a contract's spec override. Idempotent: deleting an override that does not exist still succeeds.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract whose spec override is being removed.

get.description: The authenticated tenant's identity and grants.
Recorded request, event-served and stream-time counters for the caller.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: How many days of usage history to return, counting back from today.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of contracts the tenant watches, which is the full list since this endpoint is not paginated.

post.summary: Add a contract to the tenant's watch list

200.description: The tenant's refreshed watch list. Not a 201: the response is the whole list, not the created row.

delete.summary: Remove a contract from the tenant's watch list

parameters.name: contract_id
parameters.description: The contract to drop from the calling tenant's watch list.

get.description: Contracts the indexer is following.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of watched contracts, which is the full list since this endpoint is not paginated.

post.description: Starts ingesting a contract on the next poll. When this is the first watched contract, pass confirm=true to acknowledge switching from all-contract ingestion to the explicit list.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Required when adding the first watched contract, because that changes ingestion from all contracts to the explicit list. The exact value "true" acknowledges the transition.

200.description: The newly watched contract and its ingestion frontier.

delete.description: Removes a contract from the watch list.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The contract to stop following.

parameters.name: confirm
parameters.description: Must be "true" to remove the last watched contract, because emptying the list switches ingestion back from a specific list to all contract events. Not needed while other contracts remain.

200.description: The removed contract and the resulting ingestion mode.

get.description: Events that failed to decode or persist and were set aside instead of stalling ingestion.

parameters.name: contract_id
parameters.description: Only list dead letters recorded for this contract. Matched exactly, and not validated as a strkey — a dead letter can be recorded for input the decoder could not make sense of.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of dead-letter rows matching the request's contract filter, ignoring pagination. Omitted when the count could not be computed; the page itself is still returned.

delete.description: Removes one dead-letter row once it has been dealt with.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The dead-letter row to discard.

get.description: Return ingestion, audit, pruner, RPC and decoder counters for the running indexer.

200.description: Indexer statistics, including auditor counters when active

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket connection that pushes ingested events as they
are stored. The stream starts at "now" — no replay of historical events.
The live broadcaster applies contract, event type, topic, ledger/time
range and has-value filters; pagination and historical-only query
parameters do not create a replay stream.

post.description: Register a callback and an event filter. The signing secret is returned in the response and must be stored by the caller.

get.description: Return every webhook subscription visible to the authenticated caller. Responses include the signing secret and are not cacheable.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of subscriptions visible to the caller, which is the full list since this endpoint is not paginated.

get.summary: Get a single subscription by ID
get.description: Return one webhook subscription and its current filter.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Subscription ID, as returned by POST /subscriptions.

put.description: Update a webhook subscription. Only fields present in the request body are changed; omitted fields retain their stored values.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Subscription ID, as returned by POST /subscriptions.

delete.summary: Delete a subscription and its delivery history
delete.description: Remove a webhook subscription and its stored delivery attempts.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Subscription ID, as returned by POST /subscriptions.

get.summary: List delivery attempts for a subscription
get.description: Return the delivery attempts recorded for one subscription.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Subscription ID, as returned by POST /subscriptions.

X-Total-Count.description: The total number of delivery attempts recorded for the subscription, ignoring the limit. Omitted when the count could not be computed; the page itself is still returned.

ContractID.name: contract_id
ContractID.description:
Filter by contract ID. Accepts a single Stellar contract strkey, or
several separated by commas, in which case events from any of them
match. Every element is validated: one typo rejects the whole
request rather than silently narrowing the result to nothing.

The alphabet is base32 (`A`-`Z` and `2`-`7`), so `0`, `1`, `8` and
`9` never appear in a contract ID.

EventType.name: type
EventType.description: Filter by event type. Accepts several types separated by commas, in which case events of any listed type match. An unrecognised type is rejected rather than ignored.

Topic.name: topic
Topic.description:
Exact JSON match against any topic position. Cannot be combined with
topic0..topic3 — a request carrying both is rejected, because the
two ask different questions and silently preferring one would hide
the mistake.

A value that parses as JSON is used as-is; anything else is treated
as a JSON string, so `transfer` and `"transfer"` mean the same
thing.

Topic0.name: topic0
Topic0.description: Exact JSON match against topic position 0, usually the event name. Same value rules as topic, and likewise cannot be combined with it.

Topic1.name: topic1
Topic1.description: Exact JSON match against topic position 1. Same value rules as topic, and likewise cannot be combined with it.

Topic2.name: topic2
Topic2.description: Exact JSON match against topic position 2. Same value rules as topic, and likewise cannot be combined with it.

Topic3.name: topic3
Topic3.description: Exact JSON match against topic position 3. Same value rules as topic, and likewise cannot be combined with it.

FromLedger.name: from_ledger
FromLedger.description: Inclusive lower ledger bound. Must be a positive integer; zero is rejected rather than treated as "unbounded", so a miscomputed bound cannot silently widen a query. When to_ledger is also given, from_ledger must not be greater than it.

ToLedger.name: to_ledger
ToLedger.description: Inclusive upper ledger bound. Must be a positive integer; zero is rejected rather than treated as "unbounded". When from_ledger is also given, it must not be greater than this value.

FromTime.name: from_time
FromTime.description: Inclusive lower created_at bound, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with a timezone and whole-second precision. Sub-second precision is rejected rather than truncated, because a truncated bound would quietly include or exclude a boundary event. When to_time is also given, from_time must not be after it.

ToTime.name: to_time
ToTime.description: Inclusive upper created_at bound, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with a timezone and whole-second precision. Sub-second precision is rejected rather than truncated. When from_time is also given, it must not be after this value.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description:
Page size. Out-of-range values are rejected rather than clamped, so
a caller asking for more than it may have finds out instead of
silently receiving a short page and assuming it reached the end.

The ceiling is 500. An operator can lower it with the API_MAX_LIMIT
environment variable, so a deployment may reject a value this schema
permits; the store never returns more than 500 rows in one page
regardless.

ContractsLimit.name: limit
ContractsLimit.description: Page size for the contract listing. Bounded tighter than the event endpoints, and by a compile-time constant rather than API_MAX_LIMIT, because the listing is a grouped scan over the events table — one row of output costs far more than one event does.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor. Pass back the cursor a previous response
returned, unchanged; clients must not construct, parse or modify
one, and its encoding is not part of this API's contract.

A cursor is only meaningful for the ordering that produced it.
Replaying one against a different order_by is rejected rather than
silently restarting the walk. The absence of a cursor in a response
means that page was the last one.

Order.name: order
Order.description: Sort direction for the order_by key. Cannot be combined with the recent shorthand, which pins the direction itself.

OrderBy.name: order_by
OrderBy.description: Sort key. Whichever key is chosen also decides which cursors are valid for the walk, so changing it mid-pagination means starting over. Cannot be combined with the recent shorthand.

Decoded.name: decoded
Decoded.description: Controls how stored event bodies are rendered. "true" enriches events with spec-driven named fields; enrichment is skipped silently when no contract spec is available, so a decoded request is never an error. "false" is the opt-out: the stored columns are returned exactly as they are, without the additive sep41_event envelope the default rendering attaches. Omitting the parameter, or passing any other value, keeps that default rendering.

ContractIDPrefix.name: contract_id_prefix
ContractIDPrefix.description: Match contracts whose ID starts with this prefix. This is a prefix filter, not a complete contract ID, and cannot be combined with contract_id.

TopicContains.name: topic_contains
TopicContains.description: Match events whose topics array contains the supplied JSON value using JSONB containment. The value must be valid JSON; unlike topic, bare text is not automatically quoted.

TxHash.name: tx_hash
TxHash.description: Match events emitted by this Stellar transaction hash.

TxIndex.name: tx_index
TxIndex.description: Match the transaction's zero-based index within its ledger.

OpIndex.name: op_index
OpIndex.description: Match the operation's zero-based index within its transaction.

InSuccessfulCall.name: in_successful_call
InSuccessfulCall.description: Filter by whether the event was emitted inside a successful call. Omit the parameter when either outcome is acceptable.

HasValue.name: has_value
HasValue.description: Filter events by whether they have a non-empty value field.

Recent.name: recent
Recent.description: Shorthand for the newest events. Use "true" for the default of 20, or a positive integer for a custom page size. It cannot be combined with order, order_by or limit.

Fields.name: fields
Fields.description: Comma-separated allowlist of event properties to return. Supported names are id, contract_id, ledger, type, tx_hash, tx_index, op_index, in_successful_call, topics, value and created_at. Omit the parameter to return the complete event.

IncludeXDR.name: include_xdr
IncludeXDR.description: Return the stored base64 XDR projection (topics_xdr and, when present, value_xdr) instead of the decoded event columns. The exact value "true" enables this projection.

Stream.name: stream
Stream.description: Return matching events as a streaming NDJSON response instead of a JSON page. The exact value "true" enables streaming.

Envelope.name: envelope
Envelope.description: Return list data in the common {data, next_cursor} envelope. The exact value "true" enables the alternate response shape.

Pretty.name: pretty
Pretty.description: Pretty-print JSON responses for human use. The exact value "true" enables indentation; it does not change the response data.

IfNoneMatch.name: If-None-Match
IfNoneMatch.description: Optional entity tag from a previous response. A matching tag causes a 304 response when the resource supports cache validation.

ETag.description: Entity tag for conditional requests and cache validation.

Link.description: RFC 5988 pagination links for the next and previous pages.

APIKey.description: API key metadata. The secret half of the key is never included — only a bcrypt hash of it is stored, and the plaintext is returned exactly once, by POST /apikeys.

id.description: Database ID, used to revoke the key.

name.description: Human-readable label, empty for an unnamed key.

prefix.description: The non-secret 16-character hexadecimal lookup handle stored in the clear. It identifies the key without revealing it.

revoked_at.description: When the key was revoked. Absent while the key is active.

APIKeyRequest.description: Optional body for creating an API key.

ContractSpecOverrideRequest.description: Wrapper containing a SEP-0041 contract specification JSON. Send the specification under the spec property.

in_successful_call.description: Whether the event was emitted in a successful call

topics.description: Event topic values; each item is arbitrary JSON.

network.description: Stellar network on which the event was observed.

sep41_event.description: Optional additive SEP-41 normalized event envelope. Omitted for events that do not match a SEP-41 event shape.

EventWithXDR.description: XDR-only projection returned by include_xdr=true. The projection contains the stored raw topic/value fields rather than the decoded event columns.

ProjectedEvent.description: Event object containing only fields selected by fields=.

EventsResponse.description: A page of decoded, enriched, projected or XDR events.

cursor.description: Present when more results exist; pass back as ?cursor=

EventEnvelopeResponse.description: Alternate list shape returned when envelope=true.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, omitted at the end.

EventListResponse.description: Default event page or the alternate envelope page.

EventResponse.description: A single decoded, enriched, projected or XDR event.

AddressSummary.description: Aggregate activity for one Stellar address.

Stats.description: Ingestion, audit, RPC, cache and decoder counters.

TenantUsage.description: One UTC day of tenant usage counters.

TenantAPIKey.description: Tenant API key metadata; secret is returned only on creation.

secret.description: Plaintext tenant key, returned only by the create endpoint.

WatchedContract.description: One contract in the global ingestion watch list.

SubscriptionFilter.description: Filter that callbacks use to select which events to deliver. An empty filter matches every event.

topic.description: Exact JSON match against any topic position

network.description: Restrict delivery to one Stellar network.

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant; omitted for operator-owned subscriptions.

DeliveryEnvelopeResponse.description: Alternate delivery-attempt page returned when envelope=true.

DeadLetter.description: An event that could not be decoded or persisted.

event_count.description: Total stored events for this contract

first_ledger.description: Oldest ledger with a stored event for this contract

last_ledger.description: Newest ledger with a stored event for this contract

last_seen.description: Wall-clock time the most recent event was ingested

ContractListEnvelope.description: Alternate contract-list page returned when envelope=true.

ContractListResponse.description: Default contract page or alternate envelope page.

TenantAuth.description:
The tenant API key issued by POST /admin/tenants/{id}/keys, presented
as `Authorization: Bearer st_<prefix>_<secret>`. The same key is also
accepted in an `X-API-Key` header (see TenantAuthHeader); Bearer wins
when both are present.

Only enforced when the instance runs with MULTI_TENANT=true. On a
single-tenant instance every request is served as an implicit
wildcard principal and no credential is required, which is why most
operations list this scheme as optional rather than required.

TenantAuthHeader.name: X-API-Key
TenantAuthHeader.description: The same tenant API key as TenantAuth, presented in a header instead of a Bearer token.

InstanceAPIKey.name: X-API-Key
InstanceAPIKey.description: Global SoroTrail API key used by /apikeys and, when API_KEY_AUTH_ENABLED is true, protected streaming and webhook operations. The same key may be presented as an Authorization: Bearer token; the X-API-Key form is shown here because it is the canonical management-header form.

ManagementKey.name: X-API-Key
ManagementKey.description:
The operator's instance-wide management key, configured through the
API_KEY environment variable. It gates the endpoints that mutate
ingestion or read the dead-letter queue, and it is always required on
those endpoints — independently of MULTI_TENANT, and independently of
the tenant credential above.

When API_KEY is unset the server fails closed: those endpoints answer
503 rather than running unauthenticated.

NotModified.description: The cached copy is still current. Returned for a conditional GET whose If-None-Match matches the resource's current ETag. The body is empty; the validators are repeated so the client can refresh its cache entry.

Cache-Control.description: The caching policy for the unchanged resource.

BadRequest.description: The request could not be parsed or violates a documented constraint — a malformed identifier, an out-of-range limit, an unparseable cursor, or a JSON body the endpoint cannot decode. The message names the offending parameter.

Unauthorized.description:
No credential was presented, or the one presented is malformed,
unknown or revoked.

Which credential is missing depends on the endpoint's security
requirement: endpoints requiring ManagementKey want the operator's
`X-API-Key`, while everything else wants the tenant key and only
rejects when the instance runs with MULTI_TENANT=true.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The authentication challenge, per RFC 7235 §4.1 — for example `Bearer realm="sorotrail"`. Present on the tenant-authentication failures; the ManagementKey path answers without a challenge because it accepts no Bearer token.

Forbidden.description: The credential is valid but does not entitle the caller to what it asked for: a disabled tenant, a non-admin calling an admin endpoint, or a request naming a contract outside the tenant's grants. Contract IDs are public on-chain identifiers, so a request for an ungranted contract is answered 403 rather than 404.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist, or is not visible to the caller. Event lookups answer 404 rather than 403 for an event the caller may not read, so the endpoint cannot be used as an existence oracle. The tenant and admin endpoints also answer 404 when the instance runs single-tenant and those routes are therefore inert.

Conflict.description: The request collides with the current state — a duplicate tenant name, or a tenant attempting to delete the account it is authenticated as.

TooManyRequests.description:
The caller exceeded its request quota, or asked to watch more
contracts than its quota allows.

Rate limiting is per client — keyed on the authenticated tenant where
one exists and on the client IP otherwise — and is only active when
the operator configured RATE_LIMIT_RPS or a per-tenant override. The
probe and scrape endpoints (/health, /livez, /readyz, /metrics) are
never rate limited, so throttling cannot blind an operator to the
throttling itself.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds to wait before retrying, per RFC 7231 §7.1.3. Always at least 1, and rounded up from the limiter's own wait-to-next-token estimate.

InternalError.description: The request failed for a reason the caller cannot act on — a store or RPC failure, or a panic caught by the recovery middleware. The message is deliberately generic; the specifics are logged against the request's X-Request-ID rather than returned.

NotImplemented.description: The endpoint exists but the feature behind it is not configured on this instance. Returned by the live event stream when the broadcaster is disabled.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The endpoint is temporarily unusable or not configured on this instance. The management endpoints answer this when API_KEY is unset, failing closed so writes are never open on a misconfigured instance; /metrics answers it when no metrics collector is wired in.
